title: Predicting Audience reactions for iHeartMedia

brand.name: iHeartMedia
brand.logo_note: Official iHeartMedia stacked logo, as used in the header of iheartmedia.com.

tagline: Test podcast launches, trailers and new music on a simulated iHeart audience before you commit airtime or marketing.
note: Retrospective test: Minds rated these 15 podcasts and songs on 2026-11-21, after they had launched. It is separate from the pre-registered public forecast ledger and its headline accuracy.
intro: Minds is a simulated audience built from published evidence about real people. Ask it the questions you would put to a listener panel, and get answers without recruiting one.

labels.order: Podcasts, then songs, best real-world result first

predicted.heading: Which shows and songs would listeners pick?
predicted.lead: We played 8 new iHeartPodcasts launches and 7 new songs to 30 Minds built on iHeart listeners: each podcast with its cover art and official trailer, each song with its cover and frames from a minute of its official music video. Then we compared their answers with how each title actually did: its peak in Apple Podcasts’ Top New Shows, or on the Billboard Hot 100.

podcast_launch.definition: Best (lowest) position reached in the Associated Press weekly 'Apple Podcasts – Top New Shows (US)' top-10 list (published each Monday/Tuesday) from the show's launch through the 2026-11-17 list. null = never in that top 10 in any readable weekly list after launch. Lower is better; all nulls tie below #10.
podcast_launch.sources: 13 consecutive AP weekly lists 2026-08-25 to 2026-11-17 read on wtop.com (plus the 2026-07-28 list on Yahoo for context). Lists for 2026-08-04, 08-11 and 08-18 could not be fetched (wtop/yahoo URLs 404). Launch dates are the first episode pubDate in each show's official RSS feed (Omny); descriptions are the channel <description> from that feed; artwork is the Apple Podcasts artworkUrl600 from the iTunes lookup API.

song.definition: Peak position on the Billboard Hot 100 as of the chart dated 2026-11-21, with weeks on chart; null = did not enter the Hot 100 (checked against every weekly Hot 100 and Bubbling Under chart 2026-06-20 to 2026-11-21).
song.sources: Billboard weekly Hot 100 / Bubbling Under chart pages and Billboard artist chart-history pages (billboard.com), read 2026-11-21. Songs named in iHeartMedia press releases: On The Verge (2026-07-31) and the weekly 'iHeartMedia Celebrates New Music' World Premiere / New Music Friday releases (2026-10-23, 2026-11-06). Artwork from Apple Music via iTunes lookup.

order: Podcasts, then songs; each by actual result, best first. Ties share a rank.

audience.name: iHeartMedia Listeners (US)
audience.question: Each podcast: cover art and official trailer. Each song: cover art and a one-minute clip of the official music video. How likely are you to listen? 0 to 10.
audience.description: 30 Minds modelled on US adults who listen to iHeartMedia at least monthly: iHeart AM/FM radio, the iHeartRadio app or iHeart podcasts.
audience.explainer: We built 30 Minds: simulated iHeart listeners. Each Mind is a complete person, with an age, a job, a commute, favourite radio formats, podcast and streaming habits and a voice of their own, grounded in public sources. Together they match published statistics on who listens to iHeart, so you can play them a trailer or a new single the way you would a listener panel.

example_mind.label: Example Mind
example_mind.name: Raul Espinoza
example_mind.description: Raul Espinoza is a 61-year-old full-time sales representative who offers keen insight into daily commuter listening habits. Living alone, he relies on his in-car receiver away from home, tuning into broadcast country radio for steady morning companionship. He balances over-the-air country broadcasts with curated free playlists to navigate his workday on the road.
example_mind.note: Every Mind is a full profile grounded in public sources. Meet one of the 30. Simulated, not a real person.
example_mind.sources_note: Every attribute traces back to public evidence. These are the sources behind this Mind.

values.label: Occupation Category
values.reason: No source covered this dimension for this audience, so these shares are model assumptions, not research findings. Use rework to change them. iHeartMedia's broad mass-market audio reach reflects typical occupational patterns of the US adult civilian workforce and non-working population.

attributes.label: iHeartMedia audio listening
attributes.value: listeners of iHeart-owned AM/FM radio stations
attributes.reason: US adults who consume iHeartMedia audio monthly across broadcast, streaming, and podcast platforms. Traditional broadcast radio remains the broadest reach channel for iHeart's audience, followed by digital app streaming and podcast network listenership with multi-platform overlap.
